newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open weaker after holiday weekend.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open weaker after holiday weekend.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker in quiet trade on Tuesday, mirroring losses recorded by U.S. Treasuries on Monday when fixed-income markets were closed in most Canadian provinces.

"Canada is just catching up to the U.S. from yesterday, but it's really, really quiet. The focus for the week is definitely the U.S. refunding," said Barry Allan, vice-president of global fixed-income with Altamira Investment Services Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.41 to C$120.56 to yield 6.439 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 3/32 to yield 6.49 percent. The negative spread between the bonds widened to five basis points from four basis points at Friday's close.

U.S. treasuries extended losses on Monday after Friday's sharp drop, which was prompted by strong U.S. economic data. But Canadian bonds could not match Monday's U.S. losses because it was a market and civic holiday in most provinces.
Analysts said fixed-income traders in both countries were now looking ahead to how new supply would be received by financial markets this week.
The U.S. Treasury this afternoon will auction US$16 billion in three-year notes, with an auction of 10-year notes on Wednesday and 30-year notes on Thursday.
In Canada, the federal government on Wednesday will auction C$2.3 billion of bonds due June 1, 2008.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.23 to C$109.63 to yield 5.939 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond traded unchanged to yield 6.22 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 28 basis points from 27 basis points at Friday's close.
